newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's AMP still keen on US, UK buys.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's AMP still keen on US, UK buys.

text.p: Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) chief executive George Trumbull said on Sunday the life insurance group was still keen on making acquisitions in the United States and United Kingdom.

"I'd like to believe that we'll make an acquisition, the prices are pretty steep right now, particularly in the U.S.," Trumbull said in a television interview on Channel Nine's Sunday programme. AMP is Australia's largest life insurer.
"We're of a mind that overpaying doesn't make much sense so I think it depends on the market and the opportunities," Trumbull said.

"Certainly we'd like to (buy) whether in fact we can find the right company at the right price is something I wouldn't want to predict," Trumbull said. He added AMP had the capacity to make very large acquisitions.
AMP has about A$90 billion in funds under management.
It is rumoured to be eyeing U.K. life insurance mutual Scottish Amicable, which like AMP is in the process of demutualisation.
Scottish Amicable is also subject to takeover bids from UK financial service groups Abbey National and Prudential Corp Plc.

Trumbull reiterated that AMP was unlikely to be a bidder for any major Australian bank, if the nation's bank ownership rules were loosened following the Wallis report into the country's financial services industry to be handed down in March.
He said Australia had too many bank branches and local banks had to reduce their branch network.
"To buy one of the big banks in Australia and then to go through their process (of closing bank branches) seems to us not to make as much sense as doing it in some other way," he said.
Trumbull also reiterated that AMP's proposed demutualisation was in the best interest of all policyholders.
